transcript.answer: Lore's agent pods run in Kubernetes clusters as Agent custom resources (CRs). They run in the central cluster or in satellite execution clusters, each of which has its own cluster-agent plus the ai-agents subsystem. The Floor no longer holds a Kubernetes client. Under ADR-024's 2026-08-24 amendment and ADR-044, `apps/cluster-agent` is the only process that talks to a given cluster's API, with one per cluster. The Floor and lore-api reach it over HTTP. Earlier, the Floor held a Kubernetes client for dispatch, and ADR-044 initially left Agent CR dispatch in the Floor. Later amendments moved that to the cluster-agent. Issue 891 still mentions `@kubernetes/client-node` call sites that use `loadFromCluster()`, so some of that code may predate or lag the extraction. I did not verify that.

judgements.reason: The answer says pods run via Lore's own apps/cluster-agent, which talks to the cluster API, and that Lore may still have @kubernetes/client-node call sites; it never mentions the external re-cinq/floor reached through @re-cinq/floor-client.

The answer says agent pods run in Lore's own clusters through a cluster-agent and that Lore code holds Kubernetes clients, while the gold says they run in the external floor, reached only via floor-client, and that Lore holds no Kubernetes client.
